[clock:interval].summary: Allocates a repeating monotonic timer; save its reference instead of creating one on every loop.
[clock:interval].returns: Timer reference; inspect last clock status if allocation fails.
prerequisites: Import Clock & Timers and its declared dependencies.

examples.title: Use timer every … ms
examples.explanation: Block notation: Allocates a repeating monotonic timer; save its reference instead of creating one on every loop. Timer reference; inspect last clock status if allocation fails.

examples.title: One event each second
examples.code:
set timer to (timer every [1000] ms)
repeat [3]
  wait for timer [timer]
  say [tick]
delete timer [timer]
examples.explanation: Create the timer once, consume events, then release its slot. No calendar setup is required.

notes: Timers use monotonic uptime and work without setting a calendar clock. Save the timer reference in a variable. Ready does not consume an event; take consumes it. Only one event is pending per timer; more firings coalesce. Eight timers maximum, interval 10 ms to 24 hours. Stop clears an event; restart rearms; delete releases the reference. Stop All releases all timers, so recreate them when starting again. Manual UTC uses YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (1970–2399). Offset is minutes from UTC, not a named timezone or automatic DST. Daily and UTC schedules require a valid clock. Catch up true delivers one event after a forward jump; false skips it. Daily dates never repeat after backward jumps. RTC and NTP are unavailable in this backend. Large missed counts and elapsed milliseconds saturate at 1073741823 in VM reporters. New firmware required; local build/rendering only until physical tests pass.
Source: integration\Clock_Timers.ubl. Examples are illustrative block notation, not hardware acceptance tests.
